title: The Complete Guide to Customer Reactivation for Service Businesses | Winback Engine Blog

facts.fact: Vendor's blog states that industry data shows 60–70% of a typical service business's customer base is lapsed at any given time.
facts.quote: Industry data shows that 60–70% of a typical service business’s customer base is lapsed at any given time.

facts.fact: Vendor's blog states that reactivation campaigns typically cost 5–10x less per converted customer than new customer acquisition.
facts.unit: x less cost per converted customer
facts.quote: reactivation campaigns typically cost 5–10x less per converted customer than new acquisition.

facts.fact: Vendor's blog says a 'lapsed' service-business customer is typically someone who hasn't booked in 90–180 days, with the exact threshold depending on service cadence.
facts.quote: a “lapsed” customer is typically someone who hasn’t booked in 90–180 days (the exact threshold depends on your service cadence).

facts.fact: Vendor's comparison table lists cost per contact of $50–$200 for new customer acquisition versus $5–$20 for customer reactivation.
Vendor's comparison table lists conversion rate of 1–3% for new customer acquisition versus 15–40% for customer reactivation.
Vendor's comparison table lists time to first booking of 2–8 weeks for new customer acquisition versus 3–14 days for customer reactivation.
facts.quote: | Time to first booking | 2–8 weeks | 3–14 days |

facts.fact: Vendor's blog states a lapsed customer who rebooks has a 60–70% probability of becoming active again long-term, compared with a 20–30% retention rate for newly acquired customers.
facts.quote: A lapsed customer who rebooks has a 60–70% probability of becoming active again long-term, compared to a 20–30% retention rate for newly acquired customers.

facts.fact: Vendor's guidance recommends setting the lapsed threshold at roughly 1.5–2x a service's typical repeat-visit interval.
facts.quote: set the lapsed threshold at roughly 1.5–2x that interval.

facts.fact: Vendor's table lists a lapsed threshold of 30–60 days inactive for gym/fitness studios with 2–4 visits per week.
facts.quote: | Gym/fitness studio | 2–4x per week | 30–60 days inactive |

facts.fact: Vendor's table lists a lapsed threshold of 90+ days inactive for med spas visiting every 4–8 weeks.
facts.quote: | Med spa | Every 4–8 weeks | 90+ days inactive |

facts.fact: Vendor's table lists a lapsed threshold of 120+ days inactive for pet grooming customers visiting every 6–8 weeks.
facts.quote: | Pet grooming | Every 6–8 weeks | 120+ days inactive |

facts.fact: Vendor's table lists a lapsed threshold of 7+ months since last visit for dental practices that see patients about 2x per year.
facts.quote: | Dental practice | 2x per year | 7+ months since last visit |
